newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan agency wants aid for flood-affected south.
newsitem.headline: Sudan agency wants aid for flood-affected south.

text.p: The director of a Sudanese relief agency said on Saturday he had asked the government and international aid groups to send tonnes of food and seeds to areas stricken by floods in the country's war-torn south.

Majur Nhial Makol, head of the Sudan Relief Agency, told Reuters that last year's floods had prevented 10,000 residents of 18 villages in the Bor and Pibor areas of the southern Jonglei state from cultivating food crops.
"The people are surviving by gathering wild fruits and eating water lilies," Makol said. Some people wanted to fish but did not have any equipment, he added.
For the past 13 years, the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) has been fighting the Islamist Khartoum government for autonomy of the mainly Christian and animist south.

Early this year, the SPLA joined forces with a Sudanese opposition alliance which launched a widescale attack on the country's east and south. Sudan has said Uganda is helping the southern rebels, a charge which Kampala denies.

Makol said clashes in the south had led to the massacre and looting of up to two million heads of cattle from Bor, whose Dinka inhabitants rely on the herds for their livelihood. The floods had brought diseases to the remaining herds, he added.
He also said that residents of Bor and Pibor, areas controlled by the Khartoum government, needed crop seeds and vaccines for their cattle.
